metadata.title: Everolimus and Exemestane Therapy
metadata.indication: Postmenopausal HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer without symptomatic visceral disease, after recurrence or progression following a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor.
metadata.partial_assessment_policy: Each entered value is assessed independently. Omitted domains remain unassessed and are never assumed normal.

catalogue_reconciliation.scope_note: The NCCP states that its website list is not comprehensive. This reconciliation does not assert that every possible national regimen is published online.

encoding_maturity.label: Source reconciled rule encoding · independent clinical and pharmacy review pending
encoding_maturity.scope_note: NCCP 00322 v4 blood-count, organ-function and toxicity tables, indication boundaries and component-specific actions reconciled; supplementary EU SmPC safety information distinguished from NCCP.

metadata.catalogue_source_check_scope: Current official locally advanced/metastatic breast catalogue link followed to the downloaded 00322 v4 PDF; full text and dose-modification tables reconciled.
metadata.schedule_summary: Everolimus 10 mg once daily plus exemestane 25 mg once daily continuously; no scheduled rest week.
audit_limitations: Independent clinical and oncology-pharmacy validation remains pending.
NCCP toxicity tables use CTCAE v3.0; generic v5 labels must not silently replace those criteria.
NCCP does not define a fixed CT/echo/ECG or tumour-marker interval.

source_supplements.document: HPRA Exemestane SmPC cited by NCCP 00322

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: Treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: Any dose modification should be discussed with a Consultant.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: Decision-support encoding of the current NCCP source. It does not replace the official regimen, clinical judgement, local policy, prescribing review, or pharmacy verification.

anc_x10e9_l.label: ANC
anc_x10e9_l.source_grading_note: Source-defined treatment thresholds are used directly. A newer CTCAE educational grade must not redefine these treatment bands.
anc_x10e9_l.assessment_guidance: NCCP Table 1 directly uses ANC below 0.5, from 0.5 to below 1.0, and at least 1.0 × 10⁹/L. Febrile neutropenia has a separate recovery threshold of at least 1.25 × 10⁹/L and no fever. Assess platelets and other domains separately.

platelets_x10e9_l.label: Platelets
platelets_x10e9_l.source_grading_note: Source-defined treatment thresholds are used directly. A newer CTCAE educational grade must not redefine these treatment bands.
platelets_x10e9_l.assessment_guidance: NCCP Table 1 directly uses platelets below 50, from 50 to below 75, and at least 75 × 10⁹/L. Assess ANC and other domains separately.

renal_input.reason: NCCP 00322 Table 2 specifies no routine renal dose adjustment for either component, including haemodialysis. Record the measured CrCl for renal assessment; there are no source-defined dose tiers to fabricate.

crcl_ml_min.assessment_guidance: Record the verified CrCl. NCCP specifies no routine renal dose adjustment, including dialysis; acute kidney deterioration remains a separate review concern.

stomatitis_grade.label: Stomatitis severity (NCCP CTCAE v3)

options.label: No toxicity reported
options.description: No oral mucositis/stomatitis reported.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Minimal oral symptoms; usual diet is possible.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Symptoms require a modified diet, but eating and swallowing remain possible.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Oral intake cannot adequately maintain nutrition or hydration.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences.

stomatitis_grade.assessment_guidance: Use the relevant CTCAE v3.0 term specified by NCCP Table 3. This is not an automatic grade conversion from laboratory values; assess clinical severity and attribution.
stomatitis_grade.source_grading_note: NCCP 00322 Table 3 uses CTCAE v3.0. These descriptions preserve that source version; they do not substitute CTCAE v5/v6 criteria. NCI printed page 24. Uses the oral functional/symptomatic mucositis criteria; the clinical-examination scale is separate.

options.label: Grade 2

options.label: Grade 3

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening respiratory compromise; ventilatory support is indicated.

metabolic_toxicity_grade.label: Metabolic event severity (NCCP CTCAE v3)

options.label: No toxicity reported
options.description: No metabolic adverse event reported.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Grade 1 according to the named CTCAE v3.0 metabolic term.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Grade 2 according to the named CTCAE v3.0 metabolic term.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Grade 3 according to the named CTCAE v3.0 metabolic term.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Grade 4 according to the named CTCAE v3.0 metabolic term.

metabolic_toxicity_grade.assessment_guidance: Identify the metabolic event and use its own CTCAE v3.0 criteria; glucose and lipid grades are not interchangeable. For fasting hyperglycaemia, grade 1 is above ULN to 8.9 mmol/L, grade 2 above 8.9 to 13.9, grade 3 above 13.9 to 27.8, and grade 4 above 27.8 mmol/L or acidosis. Assess clinical urgency independently.
metabolic_toxicity_grade.source_grading_note: NCCP 00322 Table 3 uses CTCAE v3.0. Choose the named metabolic term on NCI printed pages 40–42; a generic mild/moderate label is insufficient.

other_non_haematological_toxicity_grade.label: Other non-haematological toxicity (excluding metabolic events)

options.label: No toxicity reported
options.description: No other non-haematological adverse event reported.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Mild event, using the specific CTCAE v3.0 term.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Moderate event, using the specific CTCAE v3.0 term.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe event, using the specific CTCAE v3.0 term.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening or disabling event, using the specific CTCAE v3.0 term.

other_non_haematological_toxicity_grade.assessment_guidance: Document and grade the actual non-haematological event using CTCAE v3.0. Do not use this field for metabolic events, stomatitis or pneumonitis, which have separate NCCP pathways.
other_non_haematological_toxicity_grade.source_grading_note: NCCP 00322 Table 3 uses CTCAE v3.0. The general severity labels on the NCI introduction are only a guide; document the actual adverse-event term and use its specific criteria. Exclude metabolic events, stomatitis and pneumonitis from this field.

diarrhoea_grade.label: Diarrhoea severity (NCCP CTCAE v3)

options.label: No toxicity reported
options.description: No increase from the usual bowel pattern.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Fewer than 4 additional stools per day, or a mild increase in stoma output.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: 4–6 additional stools per day, IV fluids needed for less than 24 hours, or moderately increased stoma output; daily activities are unaffected.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: At least 7 additional stools per day, incontinence, IV fluids for at least 24 hours, admission, severe stoma-output increase, or interference with daily activities.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences, such as circulatory collapse.

diarrhoea_grade.assessment_guidance: Use the relevant CTCAE v3.0 term specified by NCCP Table 3. This is not an automatic grade conversion from laboratory values; assess clinical severity and attribution.
diarrhoea_grade.source_grading_note: NCCP 00322 Table 3 uses CTCAE v3.0. These descriptions preserve that source version; they do not substitute CTCAE v5/v6 criteria. NCI printed page 20.

febrile_neutropenia_grade.label: Febrile neutropenia severity

options.label: No toxicity reported
options.description: No febrile neutropenia reported.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: CTCAE v3.0: fever of unknown origin without documented infection, ANC below 1.0 × 10⁹/L and temperature at least 38.5°C. Any suspected neutropenic sepsis still needs immediate assessment under local policy.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences, including septic shock, hypotension, acidosis or necrosis.

febrile_neutropenia_grade.assessment_guidance: Any suspected neutropenic sepsis requires urgent assessment; the source grade determines the later treatment decision.

supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for oral SACT
supportive_care.mapping_basis: Oral SACT classification from NCCP V6 Table 8.
other_supportive_care: Non-alcoholic prophylactic or therapeutic mouthwash according to local policy; discuss an alcohol-free corticosteroid mouthwash during the first eight weeks.
Assess possible oral candidiasis before antifungal treatment; do not add prophylactic antifungal therapy automatically.
No routine G-CSF prescription from this source.
Consider PJP prophylaxis if systemic corticosteroids or other immunosuppressive agents are needed, particularly for pneumonitis.
Assess fracture risk and bone-health management for exemestane.
supportive_care.component_specific_note: NCCP specifies continuation of exemestane during everolimus interruption or modification unless an independent contraindication or acute clinical concern changes the plan.

indications.description: Postmenopausal HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer without symptomatic visceral disease, after recurrence or progression following a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor.

treatment_phases.name: Everolimus + exemestane · continuous
treatment_phases.label: Everolimus + exemestane · continuous
treatment_phases.duration_text: Continue while beneficial and tolerated under the consultant plan
treatment_phases.schedule_summary: Everolimus 10 mg once daily plus exemestane 25 mg once daily continuously; no scheduled rest week.

administration.notes: Same time daily; consistently with or without food; swallow whole. Individual prescribed dose may differ.
After food; swallow whole. Continue during everolimus interruptions unless a separate reason requires withholding.

baseline: FBC, renal and liver profile; urea/BUN and urinary protein
Total cholesterol, triglycerides and blood glucose
Confirm postmenopausal HR-positive/HER2-negative indication, prior non-steroidal AI and absence of symptomatic visceral disease
Review lung symptoms/history, infections and interacting medicines; assess bone/fracture risk for exemestane
regular: FBC, renal/liver profile, total cholesterol and triglycerides every four weeks or as clinically indicated (NCCP p2)
Fasting glucose as clinically indicated, with closer follow-up for diabetes or medicines increasing glucose
Review oral symptoms especially during the first eight weeks; review respiratory/infection symptoms throughout treatment
Bone-density testing and bone protection according to risk; no universal DXA interval in this regimen
monitoring.disease: Response imaging and any tumour markers follow the individual treatment plan. NCCP specifies no universal CT, ECG or echo interval. New respiratory symptoms require prompt assessment rather than waiting for the next response scan.

ctcae_standard.note: NCCP 00322 Table 3 expressly uses CTCAE v3.0. Specific laboratory cutoffs override generic grade labels.
